rationale:
Owner approves requirements revision 58 as a whole (spec gate item S5), combining the four

individually reviewed decision drafts below into one evidence record because gates/spec.json's

S5 evidence policy allows only specs/requirements.json as an artifact input:



decisions/owner-approvals/revision-58-baseline.json:
DRAFT_UNSIGNED: proposes owner adoption of requirements revision 58 as a whole — the cumulative fee remainder and minimum-quote revert (already shipped and tested by WP-02), the PegCycleVault dust fast path and quarantined DEGRADED return (already shipped and tested by WP-03), chunked payouts shipped inactive at chunk count one (already shipped and tested by WP-04), and a future re-binding of the pre-existing P1-011 dashboard deferral to revision 58's requirements content once a fresh, owner-reviewed deferral descriptor exists. decisions/task-deferrals/P1-011.json itself is left untouched, still bound to its originally owner-approved revision 56 content, and decisions/owner-approvals/phase-1-revision-55-dashboard-deferral-approved.json's real OWNER APPROVED signature is not re-pointed at any revision-58 content — check-delivery-boundary.mjs currently reports that deferral's authority as invalid pending exactly this future re-binding. This draft grants no deployment, credential, signing, broadcast, asset-movement, spending, or publication authority. It does not by itself authorize REQ-cycle-control-2, REQ-distribution-1/2, REQ-canonical-market-6, REQ-fee-accounting-8, or REQ-dashboard-2 to run live — those wait on the separate standing-authority, hookdata-relaxation, and distribution-signer-custody drafts alongside decisions/ADR-0021-autonomous-cycle-authority.md.

decisions/owner-approvals/revision-58-hookdata-relaxation.json:
DRAFT_UNSIGNED: proposes approval of REQ-canonical-market-6 specifically — relaxing CanonicalMarket.sol's single-router, mandatory-hookData binding so the standard Uniswap Trading API, any wallet's default swap flow, and any DEX aggregator can swap against the canonical pool. This revises an already-tested, previously owner-reviewed invariant (the single-router binding), so it is called out as its own separate approval rather than folded into the revision-58 baseline draft, per WP-05's scoping and the design synthesis's decision D2. Fee accrual and liability accounting are unaffected: hookData only gates buyerHkmnCredit bookkeeping, never fee collection. Full-fill-only enforcement is unchanged. This draft grants no deployment authority; the code change itself (WP-05) is a separate, parallel package with its own red-team pass gate.

decisions/owner-approvals/revision-58-standing-authority.json:
DRAFT_UNSIGNED: proposes a standing signing authority for the autonomous scheduler under REQ-cycle-control-2 and decisions/ADR-0021-autonomous-cycle-authority.md. Names the first live cap: one $25 pack purchase plus bridge fees per cycle, a maximum of 72 cycles per day, both dashboard-editable within this ceiling but never past it. Confirms the two-layer kill switch (immediate off-chain pause flag; on-chain revocation of the vault-authorizer and policy-wallet keys, checked fresh on every signing request, never cached) as the actual stop mechanism, and confirms no new on-chain pause role is added (ADR-0021 cites architecture/trust-boundaries.md TB-07 by name). This draft grants no deployment, credential, signing, broadcast, asset-movement, spending, or publication authority by itself — it is the specific grant the signer service must see signed before it will produce any live autonomous signature.

decisions/owner-approvals/revision-58-distribution-signer-custody.json:
DRAFT_UNSIGNED: proposes approval of REQ-distribution-2's distribution-signer/verifier custody split, as corrected by the owner (coordinator decision D7, MODIFIED) against the original design synthesis draft. The distribution-signer signature is produced by the worker's own automated process; the verifier is a separate, independently automated process holding its own key, designed to run on a different host from the worker, that independently recomputes the manifest's root hash and root sum from finalized chain data and signs only on an exact match. No human signs per cycle by default; an optional manual/human-signed verifier mode may exist as an operator override but is never the default path. This draft names no concrete host or operator identity for the verifier process — that assignment is a separate operational decision the owner makes before the verifier process is actually deployed, and the signer service refuses to produce a live distribution-signer or verifier signature until both this draft and decisions/owner-approvals/revision-58-standing-authority.json are signed.
